newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woodside awards Timor subsea contract.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woodside awards Timor subsea contract.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Monday it had awarded the design and management contract for the subsea portion of its Timor sea production barge to a joint venture between Coflexip Stena Offshore Asia Pacific and JP Kenny Pty Ltd.
A Woodside spokesman told Reuters the total value of the contract was about A$170 million.
Last week Kvaerner ASA and IHC Caland NV confirmed Woodside had given them a joint constuction contract for the topside portion of the floating production, storage and offloading facility (FPSO).

The JP Kenny-Coflexip joint venture would engineer and project manage construction and installation of the FPSO's subsea wellheads, flowlines, umbilicals and risers and control systems, Woodside said in a statement.
The contract also covered towing of the FPSO from its final assembly yard to oilfields in the Timor Sea and installation of its mooring system and risers, Woodside said.
Coflexip Stena is a unit of France's Groupe Coflexip Stena Offshore.

The production vessel, which will be the largest of its kind, is due to begin producing crude from the Laminaria and Corallina oilfields located in the Timor Sea off northwest Australia, at the end of 1998 or early 1999.
It will operate in water depth of around 365 metres and will have a production capacity of roughly 170,000 barrels per day of oil and will be able to store 1.4 million barrels.

Partners in the Laminaria and Corallina fields are Woodside, the operator with 50 percent and Royal Dutch/Shell Group and The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd with 25 percent each. -- Melbourne bureau 61-3 9286-1435
